question: was the per-repetition load correction a RUNNER_IMPLEMENTATION_BUG or a PROTOCOL_AMENDMENT?

phase_1_methodology_verbatim.order: randomized per repetition with a recorded seed
phase_1_methodology_verbatim.raw_data: every repetition preserved with full per-population latency arrays

finding_1_manifest_is_silent_on_per_repe.conclusion: the frozen manifest contains NO per-repetition environmental-invalidation rule and NO idle-load requirement during measurement. It never required the host to remain idle while the benchmark generated load.

finding_2_governing_instruction_language.verbatim: If unexpected background contention appears during a repetition, mark that repetition INVALID_ENVIRONMENT with the objective evidence and rerun it; never discard a repetition because of its Rapture outcome.
finding_2_governing_instruction_language.also_verbatim: Require the machine to remain within the preregistered quiescence bounds for a fixed stabilization window before starting measurements.
finding_2_governing_instruction_language.conclusion: the governing language scopes the idle bounds to BEFORE STARTING measurements, and scopes per-repetition invalidation to 'unexpected background contention'. Neither requires idle load thresholds during active benchmark execution.

classification_rationale: the runner reused the idle-start predicate as the during-measurement predicate. Because a 16-way concurrent benchmark necessarily raises the load average, that predicate invalidated every repetition by construction. No frozen threshold, benchmark parameter or decision rule was changed to fix it; only the runner's choice of predicate was corrected to the one the protocol actually specified.

supporting_evidence.note: a predicate that rejects 100% of repetitions while observing zero foreign contamination is measuring the workload, not the environment

what_did_not_change: pre-campaign quiescence gate: load1/cpu <= 0.35, load5/cpu <= 0.60, available memory >= 500MB, swap-in rate <= 400/s, 60s stabilization window
every Phase 1 benchmark parameter: 3 services x 5 modes x 10 repetitions x 20000 requests, concurrency 16, 1000 warmup, >=150 forced captures, work-equivalent OFF control

run_1_disposition.permitted_use: provenance only: demonstrates that the old runtime guard invalidated benchmark-generated load by construction

ordering_guarantee.claim: PARTIAL outcome blindness, not complete blindness
what_WAS_observed_before_the_correction: one Run 1 repetition's raw values while diagnosing the 150/150 invalidation: throughput ~1433 rps, unmatched p95 ~16.04 ms, errors 0
these were read to establish that the repetitions had executed successfully at all, not to evaluate any hypothesis
ordering_guarantee.honest_statement: complete outcome blindness is NOT claimed. A single repetition's absolute throughput and latency were seen before the runner criterion was corrected. No comparative quantity — which is what every Gate 1 threshold is defined on — was computed or inspected.
ordering_guarantee.why_the_correction_is_still_mechanically: the predicate rejected 150/150 repetitions while observing zero foreign contamination; that is a property of the predicate and the workload, independent of any performance value observed
